result.title: CADS: Measuring the Incremental Contribution of LLM Proposers in Sequential Biological Screens
result.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to guide sequential biological screens, yet standard evaluations rely on raw hit counts that conflate a proposer's value with the discovery capacity of the underlying algorithmic harness. Adaptive sampling and corrupted experimental readouts also leave standard feedback comparisons without a false-discovery guarantee. We present Certified Agentic Discovery Screens (CADS), an error-controlled measurement framework that quantifies a proposer's incremental value against an identical LLM-free loop. By integrating capped likelihood-ratio bounds, e-processes, and complete-family e-BH, CADS controls the terminal false discovery rate under the stated null and corruption conditions despite arbitrary dependence, adaptive sampling, and optional stopping. In DepMap-backed simulations, CADS exposes two evaluation artifacts: the LLM-free harness alone clears the feedback gate, and raw origin counts overstate LLM contributions because LLM picks displace fallback discoveries. On the initial 20 seeds, supplying tested-candidate history to Qwen2.5-7B shifts its net contribution from +0.35, with a 95% interval covering zero, to +2.90, with the interval above zero. This initial net effect did not persist in a 50-seed matched-quota replication. These results support net gain over an LLM-free loop, measured between separately certified sets, as the appropriate measure of proposer contribution.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CADS 这一带错误率控制的测量框架，用截断似然比界、e-process 与 complete-family e-BH，在自适应采样与可选停止下量化 LLM 提议者相对于无 LLM 基线的净增量贡献；在 DepMap 模拟中揭示两种评估假象，并发现初步净效应未能在扩量复现中保持。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相对同构基线的净增益 + 抗自适应采样与可选停止的统计控制」范式，可能为评估 VLM 中 latent/视觉分支是否真正超出旁路或消融基线的贡献提供可核查的思路，复现失败本身也提示贡献归因声明需谨慎。
